mcqs.learning_point: Understand that parallel lines remain equally separated
mcqs.question: A student thinks that two parallel lines drawn on a sheet of paper will eventually meet if extended far enough. Which statement best corrects this misconception?

options.A: Parallel lines are always the same distance apart and never meet, no matter how far they are extended.
options.B: Parallel lines may meet at infinity, so they are not truly parallel.
options.C: Parallel lines are only parallel when they are short segments; long extensions may intersect.
options.D: Parallel lines are curved lines that never intersect.

mcqs.answer: Parallel lines are always the same distance apart and never meet, no matter how far they are extended.
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines, by definition, stay at a constant distance from each other and never intersect, even when extended indefinitely. Option A states this correctly. Options B and C describe false ideas about meeting or intersecting, and D incorrectly calls them curved.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in geometric figures
mcqs.question: In quadrilateral ABCD, side AB is drawn left‑to‑right, BC goes upward, CD is drawn left‑to‑right, and DA goes downward. Which pair of sides are parallel?
mcqs.explanation: AB and CD are both horizontal (left‑to‑right) and never meet, so they are parallel. The other pairs either meet at a vertex or are not oriented the same way, so they are not parallel.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify examples of parallel lines in everyday objects
mcqs.question: Which of the following everyday objects contains a pair of lines that are parallel to each other?

options.A: The edges of a closed book when it is opened
options.B: The opposite sides of a rectangular table
options.C: The spokes of a bicycle wheel
options.D: The slanted edges of a pyramid roof

mcqs.answer: The opposite sides of a rectangular table
mcqs.explanation: A rectangular table has opposite sides that are straight and never meet, making them parallel. The opened book’s edges converge, spokes meet at the hub, and pyramid roof edges are not parallel.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish parallel lines from intersecting lines
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes parallel lines from intersecting lines?
mcqs.explanation: Statement (i) – ‘Two lines that never meet are called parallel’ – is true. Statement (ii) – ‘Two lines that intersect at a point are called parallel’ – is false because intersecting lines meet. Hence only (i) is correct.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of lines are parallel?

options.A: Two lines that cross each other
options.B: Two lines that are always the same distance apart and never meet
options.C: Two lines that meet at a right angle
options.D: Two lines that form a V shape

mcqs.answer: Two lines that are always the same distance apart and never meet
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines are defined as lines that remain at a constant distance and never intersect. Options A, C, and D describe intersecting or non‑parallel configurations.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand that parallel lines remain equally separated
mcqs.question: What does it mean when we say that parallel lines remain equally separated?

options.A: The distance between them changes as you move along the lines
options.B: The distance between them is constant at every point
options.C: They will eventually meet if extended
options.D: They are curved lines that follow each other

mcqs.answer: The distance between them is constant at every point
mcqs.explanation: ‘Equally separated’ means the perpendicular distance between the two lines is the same everywhere, which is the defining property of parallel lines. The other options contradict this definition.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in geometric figures
mcqs.question: Which definition correctly describes parallel lines, and how do they differ from intersecting lines?

options.A: Parallel lines are lines that intersect at a point; intersecting lines never meet
options.B: Parallel lines are lines that are always the same distance apart and never meet; intersecting lines cross each other at a point
options.C: Parallel lines are curved; intersecting lines are straight
options.D: Parallel lines are always vertical; intersecting lines are always horizontal

mcqs.answer: Parallel lines are lines that are always the same distance apart and never meet; intersecting lines cross each other at a point
mcqs.explanation: Option B gives the accurate definition of parallel lines and correctly contrasts them with intersecting lines, which do meet at a point. The other options are factually incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify examples of parallel lines in everyday objects
mcqs.question: Identify which everyday situation shows parallel lines.

options.A: The edges of a ladder leaning against a wall
options.B: The opposite sides of a rectangular picture frame
options.C: The arms of a clock at 3 o'clock

mcqs.answer: The opposite sides of a rectangular picture frame
mcqs.explanation: In a rectangular picture frame, opposite sides are straight and never meet, making them parallel. A leaning ladder’s edges converge, clock arms intersect at the center, and a triangle’s sides all meet, so they are not parallel.
